headline: Ukrainian delegation sets off for Russian-occupied town

sources: Ukrinform (Arakhamia Telegram + Lubinets confirmation); The New Voice of Ukraine; Ukrainska Pravda; UATV (Melania Trump Newsmax statement); Censor.NET (Fox News agreement excerpts)
fault_line: Rescue or rerouting? A delegation finally moves -- but evacuees may have to travel through Russia first.

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT for departure/ceasefire duration; PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM for aid timing] A Ukrainian delegation led by Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets set off on Oct 29 toward Russian-occupied Oleshky, per Servant of the People faction head Davyd Arakhamia on Telegram, confirmed by Lubinets. Lubinets: the ceasefire has held 54 hours without a single violation; crews are clearing mines along delivery routes ahead of the first scheduled humanitarian aid shipment on Oct 30. First Lady Melania Trump said four Newsmax journalists will cover the mission as neutral observers alongside Russian and Ukrainian humanitarian leaders. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia hoped residents could receive aid Oct 29 or Oct 30. Route dispute stands: Fox News-published agreement excerpts (via Censor.NET) say evacuees bound for Ukrainian territory go first to Anapa, Russia, then by Russian military transport to Gomel, Belarus, before entering Ukraine; Zelenskyy previously warned Russia would route people toward Russia. This is the first confirmed delegation movement after a day of 'no new movement' monitors -- prior scans recorded only the 30-hour holding position (Oct 28).
sections.what_verified: Three distinct publisher families: Ukrinform (T2, STATE-UA) + NV (T3) + Ukrainska Pravda (T3), all carrying the Arakhamia/Lubinets announcements; UATV separately carries the Melania Trump Newsmax statement.
sections.what_disputed: Serhii Bratchuk (Ukrainian Volunteer Army spokesman, via UATV) warned Russia is trying to use the situation to improve battlefield positions and legitimize Putin. Zelenskyy (TSN Oct 25): Russia 'will do everything to clear mines in such a way that these people go toward Russia and stay there.' No aid arrival or evacuation is confirmed yet -- departure is not delivery.
sections.why_matters: 54 hours, zero violations, and now the delegation moves: the one ceasefire holding in this war faces its first real test -- aid on Oct 30, expiry Nov 1.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW -- Oleshky: Ukrainian delegation sets off for Russian-occupied town; ceasefire at 54 hours with zero violations, first aid shipment due Oct 30
